persons.name: Lewis Chariton
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Chariton, Lewis' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

persons.name: E. H. Mulford
persons.note: Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. It gives a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, and it is a retrospective of 1884: a YEAR off it is documented, a MONTH is not, and it says nothing whatever about 1835. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “E. H. Mulford,” (f1839_v0080, printed page 41, ward 1, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Mulford' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins E. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

persons.name: Henry Tucker
persons.note: AN 1833 OR 1834 LIST — POLL, TAX OR MUSTER — WITH ANOTHER SOURCE. Read from directory_1843, poll_1834. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Tucker, H.” (poll_1834_108, line 277). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Tucker' agrees with the entry's forenames; 2 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

citations.citation: "Black Hawk War Veterans who Enlisted at Chicago" — the Illinois State Archives database indexing volume 1 of Ellen M. Whitney, ed., *The Black Hawk War 1831-1832* (Springfield: Illinois State Historical Library, 1970), transcribed and donated to the Archives by Fred Delap of Kansas, Illinois, and republished by the Genealogy Trails Transcription Team. 134 rows, each giving name, rank, company, place of enrollment and regiment or brigade.

transcribes.work: Ellen M. Whitney, ed., The Black Hawk War 1831-1832, volume 1 (Illinois State Historical Library, 1970)
transcribes.note: THE ORIGINAL. It prints, for each veteran, name, rank, unit, place and dates of enrollment, and remarks on his service, with unit history following the rolls. Nobody in this project has seen it: the layer actually read is the State Archives INDEX of it, which carries the name, the rank, the company, the place of enrollment and the regiment and nothing else — no date of enrollment, no remark, no service record.

transcribes.work: Illinois State Archives Black Hawk War veterans database — the Chicago enrollments
transcribes.note: 134 rows. Ninety-four of them carry the company 'INDIAN' with the Rank cell left empty; forty stand in G Kercheval's company (one CPT, one 1LT, one 2LT, 37 PVT). One hundred and thirty-three carry the regiment 'ODD', which the page's own footnote expands as 'Unassigned Colonel'; the row for ZARLEY, J W leaves that cell empty.

what_it_supplies: 134 men who demonstrably stood in Chicago in 1832 to enroll for the Black Hawk War, three years before the scene
the rank and company each man enrolled in, and the regiment or brigade he was assigned to

83 names printed WITHOUT a surname comma — the French and Potawatomi forms ('AS KE WITT', 'WAB-ME-MIC', 'BOURBONNOIS, FRANCIS SR' being of the other kind) — which is the part of the town's population this project is least able to recover elsewhere
Gholson Kercheval's company as the commonest single body of Chicago enrollments, which touches a man who signs the 1833 poll list this project already holds
what_it_does_not_supply: any date of enrollment beyond the year of the war — the index drops the dates the book prints
any residence, address, lot, trade, age or household
any evidence at all that a man was still in Chicago in 1835: enrolling at a place is presence at that place on that day and nothing more
any woman, and any man who did not enroll
the remarks on service that Whitney's volume carries, which are only obtainable from the Archives by post

citations.citation: The Chicago Democrat. Vol. I, No. 1 (November 26, 1833) through Vol. II, No. 18 (August 26, 1835). Chicago, Ill.: John Calhoun, editor and publisher. Seventy-three issues, OCR-assisted research transcriptions from page scans.
what_it_supplies: that a named trade was being carried on in Chicago in a named week, and often where
self-reported addresses, which are the strongest address evidence this project has: the advertiser was paying, and his customers had to find him
dissolution, removal and replacement notices — the only thing that keeps a documented business out of the 1835 town under the owner's ruling 3
post-office letter lists, naming residents by the hundred (ruling 1: a listed name mints a resident candidate, flagged letter_list_only)
the village and later town ordinances, printed complete — the 7 November 1833 code is the richest single item in the run
arrivals and clearances, which date the piers and the harbour as working structures
public notices that fix a building as a polling place, an auction site or a meeting place on a given day
the paper's own imprint, self-reported: the corner of South Water and Clark streets
twenty-one months of continuous weekly attestation ending three weeks before the scene date, including the issue printed on 1835-07-01
what_it_does_not_supply: any building's form, material, storey count, fenestration or dimensions — an advertisement describes a trade, not a building
the specific corner of any junction it names: 'on the corner of' does not say which of the four
anything at all from an engraving — see trap 1; the cuts are the printer's stock
proof that a business named in 1833 or 1834 still stood on 1835-07-01; that is ruling 3's survival liberty, and it is a liberty
an argument from silence, unless corpus.json shows the issues either side of the silence are both in the deposit
a reading that outranks a scan read of the same passage — see ruling 2 and the C. & I. HARMON case
a citation without an issue page and column

Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.
